For reviewers

Source: vignettes/articles/for-reviewers.Rmd
for-reviewers.Rmd

This page takes you from a clean R session to real results on public data. You need R 4.1.0 or later, and no Python or sign-up.

The two public datasets here let you test the software. They don’t reproduce the paper’s figures, which used a separate dataset.

1. Install 

install.packages(c("remotes", "SeuratObject", "arrow"))
remotes::install_github("RaredonLab/NICHESv2", ref = "main")

2. Confirm it works

This takes a few seconds and uses data that ship with the package.

library(NICHESv2)

data(NICHESv2_inputs)
obj <- create_NICHESObject(
  count.mtx = NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx,
  meta.data = NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data,
  LRM.db    = NICHESv2_inputs$LRM.db,
  mode      = "spatial",
  k         = 5L
)
dim(obj)

You should see 80 cells, 50 genes, 354 edges and 15 LRMs.

3. Get the test data

Both datasets come from SeuratData. They download once, and together take about 560 MB. SeuratData also installs the Seurat package, so this step can take a while. NICHESv2 itself doesn’t need Seurat.

remotes::install_github("satijalab/seurat-data")
SeuratData::InstallData("stxBrain")
SeuratData::InstallData("ifnb")

4. Run the tutorials

Tutorial Data Time with n.cores = 2
Spatial: mouse brain 2,696 Visium spots About 4 minutes
Non-spatial: stimulated PBMCs 13,999 cells About 1 minute, 4 GB of memory

Each tutorial’s code runs from top to bottom, so you can copy it directly into R. Results should match the printed output, because scoring is deterministic and nonspatial sampling uses a fixed seed.

For a quick check, these are the expected object sizes:

Tutorial Cells Genes Edges LRMs
Spatial 2,696 31,053 18,500 3,097
Non-spatial 13,999 14,053 87,957 1,047

The spatial tutorial stores 5,191,520 non-zero scores, and the non-spatial tutorial stores 605,973.

5. Explore further

  • Input formats shows how to use your own data.
  • The NICHESObject explains each slot.
  • Neighborhood aggregation explains the 27 aggregation columns and how subsets work.
  • Exporting to TissuePlex links to the interactive viewer.

If something goes wrong

  • A download fails: the data are served by the Satija Lab. Try again later.
  • A step runs out of memory: close other programs. The non-spatial tutorial needs about 4 GB.
  • A step feels slow: raise n.cores if your computer has more cores.
  • Something else: please open an issue.
